subject: Clarify access/audit log export formats, retention windows, and deletion process
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access/audit logs — export formats + retention windows

Diego —

We’re preparing our internal evidence packet for a HIPAA readiness review and need a couple of clarifications about Redwood’s audit/access log capabilities before we finalize our control mappings. Specifically: 

1) Export formats you can provide (CSV, JSON, Parquet, syslog push, direct S3/Bucket delivery).
2) Export cadence options (real-time stream, daily dump, weekly snapshot).
3) Retention windows you support natively versus things we must retain after export.
4) Deletion/erase process — how do you certify deletions of tenant-specific audit data? Chain-of-custody, hash verification, and whether you provide deletion receipts.

Would you also be able to point us to an export spec or example manifest? If we can get a short answered Q&A and an example schedule, we can wrap our evidence pack this week.

Thanks,
Jordan
Security Engineer — Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

--
Attachment: none in this message
From: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access/audit logs — export formats + retention windows

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, full notes below and I’ve attached a concise export spec and an export-schedule template.

1) Formats: We support JSON (newline-delimited), Parquet (columnar), and CSV. For streaming we can forward syslog/CEF to a customer collector or write to an S3-compatible bucket.
2) Cadence: Real-time event stream (pub/sub or HTTP streaming), configurable daily/weekly snapshots, and ad-hoc bulk exports on request.
3) Retention: Default hosted retention for audit/access logs is 90 days. For Dedicated/Private customers we can configure 30/90/365/1095 (3 years) or custom windows; exports are common for longer-term retention.
4) Deletion: We provide tenant-scoped deletion with an append-only deletion log in our control plane and a signed deletion receipt (SHA256 of export + deletion marker). For Private deployments, deletion is coordinated with the customer's on-prem ops and can include physical wipe steps per agreement.

Notes (details):
- Export delivery: delivery to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets uses short-lived credentials we rotate per-export. We can optionally publish to an HTTP endpoint for real-time ingestion. Parquet exports include a manifest.json with file-level checksums.
- Export schema: each record includes timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, actor (internal/external), resource path, action, outcome, and raw request/response metadata (truncated by default — full payloads are only included on forensic export).
- Retention responsibilities: exported files are under customer control once delivered; Redwood’s retention setting governs what we keep in our service. If you request a 7-year retention we recommend exporting to your long-term storage and using lifecycle rules (archive -> cold storage) on your side.
- Deletion assurance: we run an internal job that zeroes out KV caches and rotates keys; for exported data we provide a deletion receipt template you can include in an evidence binder.

I’ve attached a short spec (redwood-audit-export-spec.pdf) and an export schedule template (export-schedule-template.xlsx). If you’d like, Marissa and Neha can run through the manifest fields with your engineer and lock a cadence.

Next steps:
- Jordan: confirm preferred delivery (S3 vs syslog vs real-time endpoint) and target retention period you need for controls.
- We’ll propose a mutual action plan (MAP) and provide the signed deletion receipt example.

Diego Fernandez
Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
Diego.Fernandez@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-audit-export-spec.pdf, export-schedule-template.xlsx
From: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme Health — export choices and deletion receipts (prep for sync)

Marissa / Neha —

Short prep notes before the 2pm sync with Acme: Jordan wants export formats, retention guidance, and a clear deletion certification for their HIPAA evidence pack. They explicitly called out chain-of-custody and hash verification.

Options to present: 
- Option A (managed): daily Parquet exports to acme-prod-audit (S3), retention on Redwood side 90d, customer retains exports for 7y. We provide manifest.json + SHA256 for each file and a signed deletion receipt when they ask us to purge retained copies.
- Option B (streaming): syslog/CEF push to customer collector for real-time ingestion. Redwood retains only 30d. No exported file hashes (but we can include event sequence markers).
- Option C (private-dedicated): full-control deployment — retention/erase steps handled by customer; we provide support-run deletion receipt with process logs.

Talk track for deletion receipts: what they want is an auditable artifact that shows when we removed tenant-scoped data from Redwood persisted stores. We should show: export manifest (checksums), deletion job run id & timestamp, hashes of deleted blobs (where feasible), and signed operator acknowledgement. For hosted customers we cannot provide physical disk wipe evidence but we can provide cryptographic receipts and the job logs.

Risks / questions to raise: 
- If they require NIST SP 800-88 physical media wipe proof, we need to escalate; hosted cannot offer physical disk-level receipts.
- If they expect us to retain full request/response payloads for 7 years, we should discuss cost & privacy implications. Recommend they keep long-term copies in their archive.

I’ll run the technical bits in the call; Marissa can own the MAP language, Neha can own the deletion receipt example.

- Diego

Diego / team —

Really helpful — thanks for the spec and template. A few follow-ups after our brief review: 

- Delivery: prefer S3 (acme-prod-audit) for the initial 90-day nightly export, with a weekly Parquet snapshot we’ll copy into our long-term archive.
- Retention: we’ll ask for Redwood to retain 90 days in-platform and we’ll keep long-term copies for 7 years.
- Deletion receipts: the signed deletion receipt with manifest + SHA256 will be sufficient for the HIPAA evidence binder. If you can include an example deletion receipt, that’d be ideal.

Can you send a MAP (one-page) that lists the owners, cadence, and a short escalation path? If possible we’d like to have the MAP and a sample deletion receipt in the next two business days.

Thanks — Jordan
